entries.title: Prepayments and delinquency
entries.text: Owned-portfolio conditional prepayment rate (CPR) slowed to 11.6% from 13.7% in Q1. Separately, 60+ day delinquency eased to 4.1% from 4.2%, measured by loan count in that portfolio.

sources.location: Presentation, slide 13: Selected Operational Metrics and footnote 2

supporting_review.headline: Production offset runoff, but stock, rate and flow measures describe different servicing exposures.
supporting_review.investor_read: Management says production more than offset prepayment activity and the servicing stock continued to grow. The same slide shows a lower owned-portfolio CPR and a slightly lower owned 60+ delinquency rate quarter over quarter, alongside higher completed-modification and EBO volumes. Treat UPB and loans serviced as period-end stocks, CPR and delinquency as rates, and modifications/EBO as period flows.
supporting_review.analyst_interpretation: The combination is useful for workload monitoring: slower prepayment runoff supports portfolio retention, while modification and early-buyout activity can still change operational workload. The interpretation does not imply that any one measure caused quarterly profit.
supporting_review.speaker_note: The static deck has no speaker attribution; quotations are attributed to the issuer presentation.

entries.title: Collateral-backed liquidity
entries.text: PennyMac reported $4.0bn of companywide liquidity, including cash and borrowing capacity against pledged collateral. The 10-Q says margin calls generally must be met the same day or within one business day.

sources.location: Presentation, slide 16: Strong Balance Sheet and Diverse Capital Structures
10-Q, Liquidity and Capital Resources, printed page 75; HTML text line 3161

supporting_review.headline: The reported liquidity buffer is collateral-dependent and sits alongside short-term refinancing and margin-call requirements.
supporting_review.investor_read: The presentation reports $4.0 billion of total liquidity including cash and amounts available to draw with collateral pledged, and describes a diverse MSR and servicing-advance financing structure. The 10-Q explains that a significant amount of borrowings has 30-to-364-day maturities, that facilities are renewed ahead of maturity, and that a lender can require cash or additional collateral for a margin deficit on the notice date or within one business day.
supporting_review.analyst_interpretation: The $4.0 billion figure is total company liquidity, not cash-only liquidity and not servicing-only liquidity. For oversight, the relevant watch points are collateral availability, facility renewals, margin-call timing and the split between MSR financing and production inventory financing.

entries.title: Advance recovery, FY2025 context
entries.text: Regulatory actions can increase servicing advances and delay reimbursement. The annual filing also describes allowances for advances not expected to be recovered from insurers, guarantors or beneficial-interest holders. This is continuing risk context, not a new problem reported this quarter.
entries.review_method: Astra editorial selection; independent source review; exact annual text and source hash verified

sources.location: FY2025 10-K, Risk Factors, printed page 21; Note 3, Servicing Advances, F-13

supporting_review.headline: Servicing advances carry reimbursement, regulatory-timing and recoverability exposure.
supporting_review.investor_read: The FY2025 annual filing says advances may be delayed or increased by regulatory actions, and that some government-program loans may not be fully insured or guaranteed. It also says PFSI records a valuation allowance for amounts above expected insurer, guarantor or beneficial-interest-holder recovery. At December 31, 2025, servicing advances were reported net at $589.542 million, including a $103.574 million valuation allowance, with $406.825 million pledged to creditors.
supporting_review.analyst_interpretation: For servicing oversight, the annual disclosure makes advance needs, time to reimbursement and ultimate recoverability separate watch items. This is FY2025 structural context; it does not establish that a regulatory curtailment occurred or forecast Q2 2026 losses.
supporting_review.speaker_note: The 10-K is a filed annual report; no speaker attribution applies.

evidence.location: 10-K HTML text line 3088, Risk Factors—Risks Related to Mortgage Production and Servicing / We are required to make servicing advances (printed page 21)
evidence.quote: If a loan serviced by us is in default or becomes delinquent, the repayment to us of the advance may be delayed until the loan is repaid or refinanced or a liquidation occurs. Federal, state or local regulatory actions may also result in an increase in the amount of servicing advances that we are required to make, lengthen the time it takes for us to be reimbursed for such advances and increase the costs incurred while the loan is delinquent.

evidence.location: 10-K HTML text line 4411, Note 3—Significant Accounting Policies / Servicing Advances (printed page F-13)
evidence.quote: The Company is contractually responsible for making the payments required to protect its beneficial interest holders’ interests in the properties collateralizing their loans and may, therefore, be required to advance amounts in excess of insurer or guarantor reimbursement limits. Therefore, the Company provides a valuation allowance on the servicing advances for these amounts in excess of amounts that are expected to ultimately be recovered from the loans’ insurers, guarantors or beneficial interest holders.

evidence.location: 10-K HTML text line 4413, Note 3—Significant Accounting Policies / Servicing Advances (printed page F-13)
evidence.quote: The servicing advance valuation allowance is estimated based on relevant qualitative and quantitative information about past events, including historical collection and loss experience, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts that affect collectable amounts. The provision for losses on servicing advances is included in Servicing expense in the consolidated statements of income. Servicing advances are written off when they are deemed unrecoverable.

entries.title: Servicing expense and advance-loss provisions
entries.text: The 10-Q reports a $14.2m year-over-year increase in the servicing expense category for the quarter. Management attributes the increase primarily to loss provisions on servicing advances, reflecting larger delinquent loan balances, a larger portfolio and a higher share of loans 90 or more days delinquent. The $14.2m is the total expense increase, not a separately quantified advance-loss provision.

sources.location: MD&A, Expenses, Servicing: quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026

entries.title: Cenlar and operating leverage
entries.text: In the earnings release, CEO David Spector said technology-enabled efficiency and scale were expected to produce operating leverage as the Cenlar subservicing portfolio is onboarded. He described fee-based revenue as part of the path to long-term return-on-equity targets. These are management expectations; the statement does not quantify realized savings or steady-state cost per loan.

sources.location: CEO David Spector commentary, opening earnings-release paragraphs
